# clavis run

<p class="cli-lead">Run a command with secrets injected and output masked</p>

<div class="cli-usage">

```sh
clavis run [flags] [COMMAND [ARGS...]]
```

</div>

Start your app with the environment's secrets as environment variables.
Clavis starts the command itself, so you keep one terminal; anything the
command prints is masked, so secret values don't end up in logs.

Clavis flags go **before** the command. Everything from the first word of
the command on belongs to your command, so `--` is optional:
`clavis run rails s -p 3001` passes `-p 3001` to Rails.

Without a command, `clavis run` starts the `run:` command saved in
[`.clavis.yaml`](./clavis-yaml). `clavis init` fills it in when it
recognizes the project.

## Examples

<p class="cli-example-title">Run the command saved in .clavis.yaml</p>

```sh
clavis run
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Node.js</p>

```sh
clavis run npm run dev
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Rails, with its own flags</p>

```sh
clavis run rails s -p 3001
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Django</p>

```sh
clavis run python manage.py runserver
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Use another environment</p>

```sh
clavis run --env staging npm start
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Restart when a secret changes</p>

```sh
clavis run --watch pnpm dev
```

<p class="cli-example-title">File secrets become private temporary files</p>

```sh
clavis run --mount ./start.sh
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Use -- when your command itself starts with a dash</p>

```sh
clavis run -- -my-tool --flag
```

## Flags

<dl class="cli-flags">
<div class="cli-flag" id="flag-mount"><dt><code>--mount</code></dt><dd>write file secrets to a private temp directory and expose their paths as env vars</dd></div>
<div class="cli-flag" id="flag-no-mask"><dt><code>--no-mask</code></dt><dd>disable output masking (dangerous)</dd></div>
<div class="cli-flag" id="flag-watch"><dt><code>--watch</code></dt><dd>restart the command when the environment&#39;s secrets change</dd></div>
</dl>

## Details

- **Masking** replaces injected values in the command's output. It
  protects logs and screen shares; it is not a security boundary. Turn
  it off with `--no-mask` when you debug output.
- **`--watch`** listens for changes and restarts the command with fresh
  values whenever this environment's secrets change.
- **`--mount`** writes `file` secrets to a `0700` temporary directory as
  `0600` files, puts each file's path in the variable, and removes the
  directory when the command exits.
- **Offline:** with `cache: true` in `.clavis.yaml`, the last values are
  used for up to 24 hours when the server is unreachable. See
  [offline cache](./offline-cache).
- `clavis run` exits with your command's exit code.
